title: Heterogeneous capacity-aware rollout arbiter with progressive shadowing and auto-rollback heuristics
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build an orchestration component (Rollout Arbiter) that coordinates progressive traffic migration across heterogeneous capacity tiers and regions while preserving KV/prefix cache and minimizing cost/latency regressions. The Arbiter combines a variant-compatibility scorer, capacity-aware routing policies, and staged shadowing to validate candidate model variants before full traffic ramp. It must support tenant isolation (priority lanes), partial shadowing (0->10->50% replicas), and deterministic auto-rollback when defined signal thresholds or golden-prompt regressions are detected. The feature should be pluggable into the existing runtime routing compiler and expose clear observability and runbook hooks for on-call teams.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility scoring integrated with model registry and returns compatibility_reason codes
Policy compiler emits capacity-tier aware routing plans that respect tenant priorities
Progressive shadowing flow (0%, 1%, 5%, 25%) runnable from Console with replayed traffic hooks
Auto-rollback triggers based on p95 latency increase, error-rate, and golden-prompt regression are firing in staging
KV/prefix cache preserved for >=99% of warmed prefixes during spillover tests
Observability: per-variant dashboards, rollout timeline, and automated Canary report are available
Runbook and playbook updated and reviewed by SRE and PM
technical_notes: Compatibility score is a weighted linear model: architecture_match (0/1), tokenizer_consistency (0..1), kv_schema_match (0..1), latency_cost_delta (normalized)
Admission controller will reject routing plans with compatibility_score < 0.6 unless override tag set by Platform Ops
Routing plan includes region affinity, preferred capacity tier, and fallback lanes ordered by cost_sensitivity and proximity
Shadowing implemented as request duplication with sampling knobs; duplication respects tenant isolation and PII redaction hooks
KV cache preservation uses a cache-warm window and a best-effort cold-start de-prioritization policy to limit user-visible latency spikes
Auto-rollback heuristics composed of: sustained 5m error-rate delta > 0.5%, p95 latency delta > 20%, or golden-prompt BLEU/ROUGE regression > threshold
Simulator harness uses anonymized production traces and synthetic burst patterns to validate routing plans before scheduling ramps
Integrates with existing rollout API: extend payload with compatibility_hint and preferred_fallbacks arrays
testing_plan: Unit tests for compatibility scoring and policy compiler (target 95% coverage)
Offline simulation with 48h production trace replay under normal and burst demand
Staging canaries: 3 tenants across us-west/us-east-eu with progressive shadowing steps and automated Gatling load tests
Chaos experiment: force region eviction and verify spillover ordering and KV-preservation behavior
End-to-end smoke with Console UI toggles and Canary report generation
Failure-mode matrix validated, and SRE runbook exercises executed in tabletop run
